The FDA and CDC are investigating a new outbreak of E. coli O26:H11 infections linked to Sierra Nevada Graziers grass-fed raw milk cheese.

As of Sept. 25, there are 13 confirmed patients, more than half of whom are younger than 5 years old, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Ages range from 1 to 58, with a median of 5. Eight of the patients have required hospitalization and three have developed hemolytic uremic syndrome, which is a type of kidney failure that can also cause other serious problems including brain damage and death.

The sick people are spread across nine states coast to coast. The states with patients are California, Colorado, Georgia, Kentucky, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Tennessee and Utah. Illness onset dates range from July 7 through Aug. 26.

Public health officials are interviewing patients about the foods they ate before becoming sick. Of nine people interviewed, all nine reported eating Sierra Nevada Graziers grass-fed raw milk cheese before becoming ill.

There are likely many more sick people than the patient list reflects at this time. This is because some people do not seek medical attention and others are not specifically tested for E. coli infection. According to the CDC for every confirmed patient in an E. coli outbreak there are 26 who go undetected.

On Sept. 24, the Food and Drug Administration contacted the company to notify it about the outbreak and recommend it conduct a recall. Sierra Nevada Cheese Company LCC is working with the FDA and that same day agreed to and initiate a recall of all Graziers Raw Milk Cheeses.
